audit_result.proof_trace: The function accepts a caller-specified `receiver` parameter with no validation against `legionTreasury`; `SafeTransferLib.safeTransfer(token, receiver, amount)` (L480) transfers to the arbitrary address unconditionally. The `onlyLegion` modifier (L64-67) gates who can call but does not constrain the destination, so the property invariant `recipient == legionTreasury` is entirely unenforced. The code comment 'Transfer the amount to Legion's address' (L479) contradicts the implementation, and the same unconstrained pattern exists across all four contract implementations.
audit_result.attack_scenario: If the `legionBouncer` key is compromised, an attacker calls `emergencyWithdraw(attacker_address, token, totalBalance)` on each in-scope contract (LegionAbstractSale, LegionCapitalRaise, LegionPreLiquidApprovedSale, LegionTokenDistributor, LegionReferrerFeeDistributor), draining all token balances to an arbitrary address instead of the Legion treasury.

PROP-01b-partial-asm-005.text: emergencyWithdraw transfers to Legion treasury only, not arbitrary addresses.
